name: doloop-decorations
description: Paint doloop's where-to-look gaze on the open file, plus the daily surface: your current work's blast radius, backbone reach, and house-law departures painted ambient in the editor. Deterministic, local, non-invasive (decorates, never modifies).

commands.title: doloop: Play the gaze (the structural scan path)

walkthroughs.title: Get started with doloop
walkthroughs.description: Read code you didn't write. Paint the gaze on a file, navigate to the muscle, and follow the gaze through it — deterministic, local, nothing leaves your machine.

steps.title: Paint the gaze (CLI)
steps.description:
In your repo, run **`doloop gaze .`** — it writes `.doloop/gaze.json`, the deterministic where-to-look map. Add **`--watch`** to keep it live as you code.

[Open a terminal](command:workbench.action.terminal.new)

steps.title: Read a file
steps.description: Open any source file. doloop paints it: a **▶ beacon** where you enter, a **green bar** on the muscle (the decisions, where you dwell), everything else **dimmed** (the tendon you skip). Hover a line to learn why.

steps.title: Find where to start
steps.description:
Open the **doloop** view in the activity bar — the **Where to look** sidebar ranks files: **doors → engine room → vocabulary**. Click one to jump straight to its muscle, no scrolling.

[Open Where to look](command:workbench.view.extension.doloop)

steps.title: Watch the gaze walk the file
steps.description: Press the **▶** in the sidebar title (or **Option+] / Option+[** to step). A focus marker walks the file along the gaze — beacon, then each muscle block — skipping the tendon. That's the gaze, animated.

steps.title: The whole product
steps.description: Two more surfaces: the **web cockpit** (paste any public repo at doloop-read.fly.dev → a map you recolor by lens), and **`doloop conventions --emit`** which teaches your AI your house style by writing it into `.cursor/rules` / `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`.
